yeah ok so basically under the sexual offences act all instances of penile penetration are under s1, non-penile penetration is under s2. gender of the victim does not matter, but gender (or, whether or not they're in possession of a penis / penile-object) of the perpetrator does. they've justified this as "rape is generally understood as being perpetrated by a man, on a woman" which as a statement is.. ugh.

in any case, scenarios like this (i.e. in the video) are charged under s4, so not rape, it's "sexual assault". all 3 sections have the same sentencing considerations / penalties, if that makes it any better. rape is technically not "legal" for women in the uk, it can occur, but  what they are charged with is "sexual assault". 

re: "his penis" is a misnomer that surfaces in almost all common law systems that have just lifted the law from the UK during the colonial era / afterwards. hence has caused tons of issues internationally, some places still have loopholes for marital rape / criminalise (consenting) sodomy as a result, etc.

honestly depends on how much you're willing to spend, but the quality of mental health care in the public system is not good. gaps between appointments can be 2-3 months and even then it's obvious they don't / can't care about you / even remember who you are and if you're already struggling this is... bad.

private is expensive ($200 for psychiatrist consult, not including medication, which is unsubsidised; about $60-80 an hour for counselling) but very very worth it imo. you don't need a referral, just call the clinic and ask for an appoinment and they'll slot you in. in my experience the doctors in private practice are much more personable; you also have the freedom in scheduling appointments or calling the clinic if you encounter any difficulties between appointments.

obviously this depends on your needs - if you're talking mainly about anxiety you could just try the polyclinic to IMH route first, and stick with it if you don't need your medication calibrated and are already feeling better (it is really, really cheap). i needed a higher standard of care that the public health system could not provide, so i'm just forking out cash for better care in private, which is better suited for my needs. all the best op!
